subject: Biology
title: Beyond Mendel: Complex Inheritance
description: A quick win: understand Beyond Mendel: Complex Inheritance.

hook.text: Mendel's rules are elegant, but real genetics is often messier than peas suggest.

buildup.text: Some traits blend: red and white flowers can produce pink offspring in incomplete dominance.

discovery.text: Codominance shows both alleles at once—AB blood type expresses both A and B equally.

twist.text: Polygenic traits like height involve hundreds of genes, each adding a small effect.

climax.text: Environment matters too. Nutrition can change how tall you grow, regardless of your genes.

punchline.text: Genes set the range. Life fills in the details.

quiz.question: What is incomplete dominance?
options: Traits blend, producing an intermediate phenotype
One allele completely hides the other
Both alleles show fully at the same time

details.summary: Many traits do not follow Mendel's simple dominant-recessive rules. Incomplete dominance, codominance, polygenic inheritance, and epistasis create a spectrum of outcomes far more complex than Mendel's peas suggested, explaining why most human traits are not either-or.
details.whyItMatters: Complex inheritance explains why human traits like height, skin color, and disease risk involve many genes interacting with environment. Understanding this complexity is essential for interpreting genetic test results accurately.
takeaways: Incomplete dominance produces intermediate phenotypes like pink flowers
Polygenic traits like height involve many genes each with small effects
Epistasis means one gene can mask or modify the effects of another

faq.question: Why are most human traits not simply dominant or recessive?
faq.answer: Most traits are influenced by many genes, each with small effects, plus environmental factors. Height involves hundreds of genes interacting with nutrition. This polygenic inheritance produces continuous variation rather than the discrete categories Mendel studied.

faq.question: What is the difference between incomplete dominance and codominance?
faq.answer: In incomplete dominance, the heterozygote shows a blended intermediate phenotype, like a red and white flower producing pink offspring. In codominance, both alleles are fully expressed simultaneously, like AB blood type showing both A and B antigens.
